title: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight
title_zh: 蝙蝠运动皮层在自然灵巧飞行中的高维群体编码
abstract: Elucidating the neural computations underlying natural, complex movement remains a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Bat flight presents a formidable motor control challenge, requiring hand-like wings whose many degrees of freedom must be precisely coordinated to enable rapid three-dimensional (3D) maneuvers. Here, we performed large-scale wireless recordings from the wing motor cortex of freely flying bats, combined with 3D tracking of wing kinematics. Despite the complexity of flight control, bats repeatedly executed accurate flights through precise adjustments of individual wingbeats. Surprisingly, motor cortical activity was not dominated by the wingbeat cycle. Instead, neurons were sparsely active, exhibiting mixed selectivity for flight kinematics and variable entrainment to the wingbeat phase reaching millisecond-scale precision. This yielded a high-dimensional population code driven by successive wingbeats occupying distinct neural states. These findings reveal a mode of motor cortical population dynamics expressed during natural dexterous movement that is not well captured by prevailing views derived from constrained paradigms.
abstract_zh: 阐明自然复杂运动背后的神经计算仍是神经科学的根本挑战。蝙蝠飞行提出了严峻的运动控制难题，需要像手一样的翅膀，其众多自由度必须精确协调，以实现快速的三维（3D）机动。我们在自由飞行的蝙蝠翅膀运动皮层进行大规模无线记录，并结合翅膀运动学的三维跟踪。尽管飞行控制极为复杂，蝙蝠仍通过对单个翅膀拍动的精确调整反复完成准确飞行。令人惊讶的是，运动皮层活动并未被翅膀拍动周期主导。相反，神经元稀疏活跃，表现出对飞行运动学的混合选择性，并对翅膀拍动相位呈现可变的耦合，精度可达毫秒级。这产生了由连续翅膀拍动驱动的高维群体编码，形成了占据不同神经状态的序列。研究结果揭示了自然灵巧运动中运动皮层群体动力学的一种模式，该模式并未被传统受限范式所充分捕捉。
